entry.title: Introducing Swurl
entry.summary: Swurl opens every link you click in the right browser and profile, chosen by rules in one YAML file, and it is not released yet.
entry.content:
Swurl is a link router for macOS, made by RoundRect. It becomes your default browser, and every link you click in another app, such as Mail, Slack or a terminal, opens in the browser and profile your rules choose. It is not yet released: there is no download and no install command yet.

What it is#

Swurl comes in two parts:

  • Swurl.app, a menu bar app that receives the links you click.
  • swurl, a command line tool that routes links the same way and explains why.

It requires macOS 15 (Sequoia) or later.

How it works#

Rules live in one YAML file. They are tried in order, and the first one that matches decides:

A rule can match on the address, the app the link came from, the keys you are holding and the apps that are running. Chrome, Edge, Brave and other Chromium browsers open straight into the profile a rule names.

When no rule decides, a wheel of your browsers and profiles appears at the pointer. Holding ⌥ as you click brings it up whatever the rules say.

To see which rule would match a link, without opening anything:

Swurl only becomes your default browser when you ask it to, and it can put your previous default back. It makes no network connections of its own and has no analytics.

Hearing about the release#

There is no mailing list. When Swurl is released, the news will be on this blog and in the Atom feed. The Swurl page has the details in the meantime.

entry.title: Introducing Shorty
entry.summary: Shorty manages the menu keyboard shortcuts on your Mac from one YAML file, and it is not released yet.
entry.content:
Shorty manages macOS menu keyboard shortcuts, the ones in System Settings → Keyboard → Keyboard Shortcuts → App Shortcuts, from one YAML file. It is made by RoundRect, and it is not yet released: there is no download and no install command yet.

What it is#

Shorty comes in two parts that do the same job:

  • Shorty.app, a menu bar app with an editor for the file. It syncs again whenever the file changes.
  • shorty, a command line tool that does everything the app does.

It requires macOS 15 (Sequoia) or later.

How it works#

A shortcut names a menu item and a key combination:

Menu titles are picked from the app's real menus rather than typed, and existing titles are checked against them. A New Tab where Chrome says New tab, a missing …, or an item the developer renamed is caught and can be fixed in one click.

You can put shortcuts into groups and switch a group on and off, import the shortcuts you already have at any time, and write shortcuts for apps that are not installed yet. Shorty holds those until the app shows up.

Shorty only touches shortcuts it created, or that you declared in the file. Shortcuts you made by hand stay as they are.

Hearing about the release#

There is no mailing list. When Shorty is released, the news will be on this blog, and the Atom feed will carry it. The Shorty page has the details in the meantime.
